about: MUTATING — deletes the Failed pods nothing else collects (Kubernetes' terminated-pod GC threshold is 12500, the dev session cannot delete pods, and undeclared-objects.sh leaves Pod out of scope on purpose; six evicted boss-dev pods had piled up by 2026-09-23). Asked for by David 2026-09-23 (backlog 85889a52: on a period regardless, and ad hoc) in the shape of design 17835005 (decided by David 2026-09-21 — a rendered plan hash, signed with his passkey, single-use, verified before the argv is built), and authorised per run by that passkey. Its plan is rendered by the read-only `plan-a-pod-reap`. It declares requires_approval and names that plan verb as its plan_verb, so the runner renders the plan onto the request's approve step, runs this only after a passkey signs it (a presence stamp bound to the plan bytes, under ten minutes old, single-use), and hands the script sha256 of the SIGNED plan (backlog fd7090cc). Its bound is by construction of the ONE script it calls (infra/forge/reap-terminated-pods.sh): the scope is derived (Failed, not Job-owned, not already deleting, failed more than an hour before the render, in a namespace the tree owns), never a parameter; the one argument is the approved plan's sha256, required; it re-renders and acts only on the set whose plan still hashes to that value, so a planned pod that is gone, replaced or changed deletes nothing (exit 78) — which also makes a second run of an applied plan a refusal, at most once — and a pod that failed after the plan was rendered is not in the signed set and is not deleted; it prints the plan (the capture before the delete), deletes each pod with a uid precondition the API server enforces, and reads each back.
